summary: This article explains how wind forms ocean waves, how a board's buoyancy and balance let a surfer catch and ride them, and how surfers read wave patterns to find the best wave.
introduce: Show the title “Surfing: Riding the Waves” and give pairs one minute to list everything they already know about this topic. Share a few ideas on the board, then tell students to check which ideas the article confirms.

keyTerms.def: a group of waves that travel together across the open sea
the upward push of water that helps objects float
a steady flow of water moving in one direction

challengeTerms.def: the force an object has because it is moving, which depends on its speed and mass
the force that pulls objects toward the Earth
a force that slows an object when it rubs against another surface

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that reading the ocean well is just as important to surfing as standing on the board? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Imagine you are explaining surfing to a beginner. Describe how a swell becomes a wave a surfer can ride.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review swell, buoyancy, and current, and let weak readers use a K-W-L chart and read the article with a partner.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use momentum, gravity, and friction in a short paragraph that connects the article to something they learned in another subject.
